stemOverrides.3: Car B overtakes another car A at a relative speed of \(40\text{ }ms^{-1}\). How fast will the image of car B appear to move in the mirror of focal length \(10\text{ }cm\) fitted in car A, when the car B is \(1.9\text{ }m\) away from car A?
stemOverrides.6: An electric appliance supplies \(6000\text{ }J/min\) heat to the system. If the system delivers a power of \(90\text{ }W\), how long would it take to increase the internal energy by \(2.5\times10^{3}\text{ }J\)?
stemOverrides.17: The initial mass of a rocket is \(1000\text{ }kg\). Calculate at what rate the fuel should be burnt so that the rocket is given an acceleration of \(20\text{ }ms^{-2}\). notes.3: Source dropped the leading digit of the relative speed ('0'); back-solved to 40 m/s (convex mirror image speed = m²v, m = f/(u+f) = 0.05 → 0.0025×40 = 0.1 m/s = option D).
notes.6: Source dropped the power ('0 W'); back-solved to 90 W (6000 J/min = 100 J/s; dU/dt = 100−90 = 10 J/s → 2500/10 = 250 s = 2.5×10² s = option A).
notes.17: Source dropped the mass ('000 kg') and acceleration ('0 ms⁻²'); back-solved to 1000 kg + 20 m/s² (dm/dt = M(g+a)/u = 1000×30/500 = 60 kg/s = option D).

authoredSolutions.9: Each of the first two NAND gates has both inputs tied, so they act as inverters: \(X=\bar A\), \(Y=\bar B\). The final AND gate gives \(Z=\bar A\cdot\bar B=(A+B)'\) (De Morgan) — a NOR operation. Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.13: Inside the solid conducting sphere the field is zero; in the gap between the sphere and the shell it falls as \(\frac{1}{r^{2}}\) (\(E=\frac{kq}{r^{2}}\)); the potential is constant inside each conductor and continuous across the gap. The graph showing \(E=0\) inside, a \(1/r^{2}\) decay in the gap, and the corresponding step-and-decay potential is option (A).
authoredSolutions.35: \(SOCl_2\) with methanol esterifies the carboxylic acid (via the acid chloride), converting the \(-COOH\) of tryptophan to its methyl ester \(-COOCH_3\); the amino and indole groups are untouched. So the major product is tryptophan methyl ester. Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.36: Isoprene is a conjugated diene, so HBr adds 1,4 (Markovnikov, the thermodynamically favoured product): \(H\) to C1 and \(Br\) to C4 gives 1-bromo-3-methylbut-2-ene, \((CH_3)_2C{=}CH{-}CH_2Br\). Hence option (A).
authoredSolutions.39: With excess bromine water (polar medium), phenol is poly-brominated to 2,4,6-tribromophenol (A). With \(Br_2\) in \(CS_2\) (non-polar) at \(<5^{\circ}C\), mono-bromination is controlled and gives mainly the para product, 4-bromophenol (B). Hence option (B).
authoredSolutions.47: Both \(-COOH\) and \(-NO_2\) are meta directors, so install one first to set the meta relationship. Nitration (\(HNO_3/H_2SO_4\)) gives nitrobenzene; the meta-directing \(-NO_2\) sends \(Br_2/AlBr_3\) to the meta position; then \(Mg/\)ether, \(CO_2\), \(H_3O^+\) (Grignard carbonation) converts that \(C\text{-}Br\) to \(-COOH\), giving 3-nitrobenzoic acid. Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.48: Statement I is true: in a Frenkel defect an ion leaves its lattice site (creating a vacancy) and occupies an interstitial site, so it is both a vacancy and an interstitial defect. Statement II is false (Frenkel defects occur in ionic solids with low coordination number and a large size difference between ions, not the property stated). Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.50: Free-radical bromination is highly selective for the weakest (tertiary) C–H bond. Isobutane has one tertiary hydrogen, so \(Br_2\)/light abstracts it preferentially, giving 2-bromo-2-methylpropane (tert-butyl bromide) as the major product. Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.79: Reflecting \(A(-3,1)\) in the angle bisector of \(C\) (\(7x-4y-1=0\)) gives a point \(A'\) on line \(CB\); intersecting that line with the median through \(B\) (\(2x+y-3=0\)) and the bisector locates \(B\) and \(C\). Computing the directions of \(CA\) and \(CB\) at \(C\) gives \(\tan\theta=\tan(\angle ACB)=\frac{4}{3}\). Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.80: For the implication to be false, the antecedent must be true and the consequent \(p\land q\) false. From \(\sim r\) true, \(r=F\); then \(q\to r\) true forces \(q=F\); and \(p\lor q\) true then forces \(p=T\). These give \(p\land q=F\), so the implication is indeed false. Hence \(p,q,r=T,F,F\) — option (C).
